page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 209.78 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. CPU performance is supported by AVX-512 vector extensions, yielding strong results in the PassMark CPU extended instructions test and software compilation with Clang. However, multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores sit in the middle tier.

The instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, providing a qualitative advantage for applications requiring massive RAM footprints alongside high-frequency single-core execution. However, a notable tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O must traverse the network. Additionally, while prompt processing for small and medium LLMs is average, text generation speeds are weak, reflecting the lack of GPU acceleration.

This configuration is well-suited for large in-memory databases, high-throughput memory caching layers, electronic design automation, and relational database workloads that demand high memory-to-vCPU ratios and fast single-core clock speeds.
